reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer (packet-only: competency text + rendered samples, no generator source), 2026-07-27 re-review batch

samples_reviewed.question_text: What is the total value of 1 ₱5 coin and 1 ₱1 coin?
What is the total value of 1 ₱10 coin, 1 ₱5 coin, and 1 ₱1 coin?
Compare the numbers: 10 ___ 6. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?
Compare the numbers: 18 ___ 30. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?
What is the total value of 1 ₱10 coin and 2 ₱5 coins?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Three of five seeds (42, 43, 46) ask 'What is the total value of ...', which is addition rather than comparison. The two seeds that do compare, 'Compare the numbers: 10 ___ 6' (seed 44) and 'Compare the numbers: 18 ___ 30' (seed 45), strip the money context out completely and compare bare numerals.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: No sampled item ever sets two denominations side by side, for example a ₱5 coin against a ₱10 coin, or two ₱5 coins against one ₱10 bill. The '=' relation is never keyed in any sample, and bills up to ₱100 appear nowhere in the set.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The distractor 'cannot be determined' at seeds 44 and 45 is an abstract metacognitive phrase pitched well above Grade 1 reading level, and it is transparently implausible since both numerals are printed in the stem.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Only the > and < relations are exercised, with no equal-value case, no 'which is worth more' phrasing, and no ordering of three denominations from least to greatest, so most logical variations of a comparison task are simply not produced.

competency_alignment.rationale: Interleaving money-addition items with abstract numeral comparison builds neither skill cleanly, and nothing in the seed sequence moves a learner from comparing like denominations toward comparing unlike coin-and-bill sets, which is what this lc requires.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The values compared at seed 45, 18 and 30, are not Philippine denominations at all; there is no ₱18 coin and no ₱30 bill, so the numbers fall outside the denomination set the competency names even before the ₱100 ceiling is considered.
